title: Senior AI Engineer – Agentic RAG Product Assistant for Hardware Distributor
description:
We are seeking a senior AI engineer or small development team to help architect and build an Intelligent Product Assistant for Florida Hardware Company, a long-established hardware distributor with 35,000+ SKUs, five warehouses, and a complex product/catalog environment.

This is not a basic chatbot project. We are looking for a partner with real experience building production-grade RAG / AI agent systems that can retrieve from structured product data, technical PDFs, and connected business systems while maintaining high accuracy and cost efficiency.

Project goal

Build an AI-powered assistant that can support customers and internal staff with:

product discovery and recommendations

technical product questions

safety data, labels, and installation instructions from PDFs

account-related lookups such as orders and invoice history

The assistant will ultimately integrate into our customer-facing web portal and support roughly 800 daily unique users.

What we need

We want a system that is:

accurate

cost-efficient

model-agnostic

able to support both proprietary APIs and local/self-hosted models

designed with strong guardrails to reduce hallucinations and bad recommendations

Core requirements

The solution should support the following:

1. Product catalog integration

Retrieve from a live XML/database-backed product catalog of 35,000+ SKUs

Ensure recommendations are grounded in real catalog data

2. Technical PDF processing

Read and extract relevant information from product attachments such as:

SDS / safety data sheets

labels

installation instructions

technical documents

3. API / backend connectivity

Connect to existing ERP / web systems for account-related data such as:

order history

invoice history

other account lookups as appropriate

4. Agentic orchestration

Support multi-step reasoning / tool use such as:

check catalog for SKU

find relevant PDF or attachment

validate result

generate final answer

5. Deterministic guardrails

Implement a verification layer so that any recommended SKU must be validated against the live catalog before a response is shown

6. Multi-provider model routing

Support switching between providers such as:

OpenAI

Anthropic

Ollama / local open-weight models

We want flexibility to test for the best mix of:

accuracy

latency

cost

Preferred stack / experience

We are open to your recommendation, but we are especially interested in candidates with hands-on experience in areas like:

Agentic RAG

LangGraph, LangChain, n8n, or similar orchestration frameworks

vector databases / retrieval systems

Python backend development

PDF / document parsing pipelines

API integrations with ERP / business systems

multi-model routing

evaluation frameworks / golden datasets

hallucination prevention / guardrails

Ollama or local model deployment

What makes a strong candidate

Please apply only if you can demonstrate experience with real-world AI agent or RAG systems, not just simple chatbot wrappers.

We are specifically looking for people who can show:

prior work building tool-using AI systems

experience retrieving from both structured data and documents

a thoughtful approach to accuracy, validation, and hallucination prevention

understanding of cost control and token optimization

ability to recommend a practical architecture, not just code to a prompt

In your proposal, please include

Please answer these directly:

Describe a similar RAG or AI agent system you have built.

What tech stack would you recommend for this project and why?

How would you structure retrieval across:

catalog/database data

PDFs / technical attachments

ERP / account data

How would you evaluate system performance before launch?

Have you worked with LangGraph, LangChain, Ollama, or self-hosted/open-weight models?

What would you propose for a Phase 1 plan in the first 30–60 days?

Project structure

We expect this to begin as an initial paid phase focused on:

discovery

architecture

prototype / proof of concept

evaluation plan

implementation roadmap

Successful delivery may extend into a broader implementation and go-live phase.

Engagement details

Experience level: Expert

Project scope: Medium

Duration: 1–3 months initial phase, with potential extension

Hourly preferred

To filter out generic applicants

“Agentic RAG for distribution”

so we know you read the post.

title: Senior AI Agent Engineer — Build Self-Improving Agent to Beat GAIA Benchmark Record (90%+)
description:
The Challenge

  We have a production AI agent ranked top 5% on the GAIA benchmark (#149 of 3,007 agents, 74.09% overall). The current engineer built it from 19% to 74% but has hit an architectural ceiling and is stepping back.

  Leaderboard: https://huggingface.co/spaces/gaia-benchmark/leaderboard

  We don't want incremental improvements. We want to break 90% overall and beat the current #1 L3 score of 87%. The top score globally is 91.69%.

  This isn't a prompt engineering gig — it's an AI systems architecture problem. We believe the path to 90%+ is building an agent that can diagnose and fix its own failures, not just a human manually tuning prompts.

  Current Scores vs Target:
  - Overall: 74.09% now → 90%+ target (vs #1 at 91.69%)
  - L1 (easy): 81.72% now → 90%+ target (vs #1 at 98.92%)
  - L2 (medium): 73.58% now → 85%+ target (vs #1 at 88.68%)
  - L3 (hard): 61.22% now → 80%+ target (vs #1 at 87.76%)

  What's Already Built (you're not starting from scratch):
  - Multi-agent orchestrator (Claude Opus 4.6) + 4 specialist sub-agents (Lookup, Computation, File Analysis, Critic)
  - 18 MCP tools: 7 search APIs (Tavily, Serper, Perplexity, Jina, Wikipedia, arXiv, Wayback), E2B code sandbox, Playwright browser, CustomGPT RAG
  - Hook system: budget enforcement, loop detection, safety gates, audit logging
  - Experience database: curated lessons from past failures injected at runtime
  - Hints system: pre-task analysis for traps, format requirements, pitfalls
  - Full benchmark run logs (466 tasks, 3,138 historical runs, all classified by type/domain/difficulty)
  - ~4,300 lines Python, Claude Agent SDK, FastMCP

  What We Need You To Build

  Our CEO's directive: have AI figure out the architecture to hit 95%, not have a human figure it out. Specifically:

  1. Programmatic Debugger / AI Self-Improvement Loop — Analyze failure traces from the 26% of tasks we get wrong. Automatically diagnose root causes and suggest (or implement) remediations. This creates an automated hill-climbing loop: run benchmark → analyze failures → generate fixes → re-run. This is the #1 priority.
  2. Error Correction / Doubter Loop — A classifier that detects when the agent is going down the wrong path mid-execution. If on track, continue. If off track, activate a recovery/correction loop. Top agents all have this — we don't yet.
  3. Multi-Model Integration — Route sub-problems to specialized models (O3 for math reasoning, Gemini for vision, etc.). Currently all-Claude stack — that got us to 74% but the ceiling requires model  diversity.
  4. Adversarial Critic Pipeline — Current critic is too agreeable. Need reject-by-default verification, multi-model consensus, weighted rubrics.
  5. Fix L1 Regression — Easy tasks failing non-deterministically. Agent has no memory across tasks. Reduce oscillation.

  The Hard Problems (why L3 fails at 61%):
  - Multi-step historical research questions (3+ document chains, 7+ iterative loops)
  - Agent gets lost or hallucinates toward the end of complex reasoning chains
  - 1-hour timeout per question — some tasks run out of time
  - Subtle numerical precision errors (0.0429 vs 0.0424)
  - Content accuracy: picking wrong data sources when multiple exist

  You Should Have:
  - Deep experience building agentic AI systems (not chatbots — multi-agent tool-using systems with self-correction)
  - Track record of optimizing AI systems against benchmarks (GAIA, SWE-bench, SimpleEval, or similar)
  - Strong Python — the codebase is well-structured but you need to move fast
  - Experience with Claude API / Anthropic SDK (or willing to ramp quickly)
  - Understanding of error correction, self-improvement loops, and agent evaluation methodologies
  - Comfort with multi-model architectures (Claude + OpenAI + Google)

  Bonus:
  - Published work or open-source contributions in agentic AI
  - Experience with E2B sandbox, MCP tools, or Langfuse
  - Familiarity with the GAIA benchmark specifically

  How We Work:
  - Sprint-based: benchmark score is the only metric that matters — we measure progress by official GAIA leaderboard submissions
  - Daily async updates, weekly debrief calls with PM
  - Full access to codebase, all historical benchmark logs, failure analysis, and experience database
  - Existing engineer available 10 hrs/week for handoff and maintenance questions

  We are not looking for someone who will make spot fixes that move us from 74 to 75. We need someone who can design the architecture that gets us to 90+.

title: Python Developer – Webhook Integration Test Assignment (Paid, 3-5 hrs)
description:
PAID TEST ASSIGNMENT
VenueSuite → MEWS Revenue Sync
Python · FastAPI or Django · REST APIs · Scheduled Jobs

Budget
€200–300 fixed price
Effort
3–5 hours
Deadline
5 business days after we agree
Deliverable
GitHub repo + README


→
This is a paid test assignment. We are not primarily looking for a perfect end product — we want to see how you approach a problem, how you communicate when something is unclear, and whether you can make sensible decisions independently.



1. Who We Are
We are Synrfy, a small Dutch company that builds integration and AI software for the hospitality industry. We connect hotel systems — property management, meetings & events, finance — so hotels don't have to do that manually.

This assignment is a first step. If it clicks, there is a realistic chance of follow-up work: we have multiple active integration projects and we're looking for a developer we can work with structurally. We're not promising anything, but we don't run test assignments for fun either.


2. What This Is About
Hotels report revenue on an accrual basis — revenue is recognised on the day it is consumed, not when it is invoiced. When a hotel hosts a conference through VenueSuite (their Meetings & Events platform), the daily transactions — room hire, F&B, AV equipment — need to end up in the correct account in MEWS (their Property Management System) before the night audit runs.

That sync doesn't happen automatically. Your job is to build the service that makes it happen.

The data flow is:

VenueSuite (staging)  →  your sync service  →  MEWS account

→
Revenue must be posted per event per day — not aggregated. A hotel with three events on Tuesday expects three separate account postings in MEWS for Tuesday, not one lump sum.



3. The Assignment
Build a Python service that runs daily and syncs event transactions from VenueSuite into MEWS. The service has three steps:

Step 1 — Fetch daily transactions from VenueSuite
Call the VenueSuite staging API to retrieve all event transactions for a given date.
Each transaction belongs to an event, which is linked to a booking. A booking has a reference number that ties it to a MEWS reservation.
Credentials for the VenueSuite staging environment will be shared with you separately after agreement.
Relevant data per transaction: event_id, booking_reference, date, category (e.g. F&B, AV, Room), description, quantity, unit_price.

Step 2 — Resolve or create the MEWS account
Use the booking_reference to look up the corresponding reservation in MEWS via the Connector API.
Check whether a billing account already exists for that reservation.
If no account exists yet, create one before posting transactions.
MEWS Connector API demo credentials are publicly available in their documentation — you do not need credentials from us for this step.
MEWS demo environment: https://app.mews-demo.com
MEWS Connector API docs: https://mews-systems.gitbook.io/connector-api

Step 3 — Post transactions to MEWS
Map each VenueSuite transaction category to a MEWS service or accounting category. Define this mapping in a config file — not hardcoded in business logic.
Post each transaction as a charge on the resolved MEWS account.
If a category is not in the mapping, use a configurable fallback and log a warning. Never fail silently.
Once a transaction is successfully posted, mark it as such locally. Re-running the sync must never double-post.
If a single post fails, log the error and continue with the remaining transactions — do not abort the run.

Scheduling
The sync must run on a daily schedule, timed to run just before the night audit (configurable time).
Use APScheduler, Celery Beat, or Django management command with cron — your choice. Briefly explain it in the README.
Also expose a POST /sync/run endpoint to trigger the sync manually for a given date (for testing).


4. Technical Requirements
Python 3.10+
FastAPI or Django REST Framework — your choice. Explain briefly in the README.
SQLite is fine for local state (posted transactions, sync logs).
Use an ORM — no raw SQL.
Category mapping in a config file (YAML or JSON), not in application code.
Single startup command: uvicorn main:app --reload or python manage.py runserver.
requirements.txt or pyproject.toml included.


5. Access & Credentials
VenueSuite staging API: credentials shared separately after we agree. You will receive a base URL, API token, and a property ID to work with.
MEWS demo: use the public demo credentials from the MEWS Connector API documentation. No setup needed.

→
If you run into access issues with either system, message us immediately — don't spend hours on workarounds. We'll fix it.



6. Deliverables
Working Python codebase covering all three steps.
Category mapping config file with at least F&B, AV, and Room Hire mapped.
README: how to run locally, how to trigger a manual sync, your framework and scheduler choice explained in a few sentences, any known limitations.
A curl.sh or .http file to trigger the manual sync endpoint.


7. What We Actually Look At
What we look at
Why it matters
Communication
Do you ask questions before you start? If something is unclear, do you message us or just guess and push forward? This matters more than anything else.
Independent thinking
Can you make a reasonable decision — framework, scheduler, error strategy — and explain it briefly? We don't want a thesis. Two sentences is enough.
Correct flow
Data moves from VenueSuite into MEWS, per day, per event. Account creation is handled automatically. This is the core logic — get this right.
Idempotency
Re-running the sync for the same date must never double-post. We will test this.
Error handling
What happens when a category is unmapped? When MEWS returns a 429? When a VenueSuite call times out? We want to see you thought about it.
Code clarity
Readable structure, sensible naming, logic not living in route handlers. Someone else should be able to read it without asking you to explain it.



8. Practical Notes
There is no single right answer. We're more interested in your reasoning than your solution.
If something in this document is unclear, message us before you start — not halfway through.
We review every submission personally. You'll get feedback either way.
Do not share or publish the VenueSuite staging credentials.



Questions before you start? Reach out — we prefer a short conversation over re-work.

title: MVP Development – SMS-Based Daily Check-In and Alert System
description:

Project Overview
We are seeking an experienced developer or small development team to build the MVP for a SaaS platform that provides a scheduled SMS check-in system with automated escalation if the user does not respond.
The goal of the MVP is to create a reliable system capable of sending daily check-in messages to users, processing responses, and notifying a designated contact if the user fails to respond.
Target development timeline: 4–8 weeks.

Core Functional Requirements
User Registration
Users must be able to create an account and provide the following information:
Name
Phone number
Time zone
Preferred daily check-in time
Emergency contact name and phone number
Users will subscribe to a monthly plan using Stripe.

Scheduled SMS Check-In
The system must automatically send a daily check-in message to each user at their chosen check-in time.
The system must be able to send scheduled messages across multiple time zones.

SMS Response Processing
The system must receive and process replies to the SMS message.
If the user replies YES:
record response
mark the daily check-in as completed
If the user replies NO:
notify the emergency contact via SMS

Missed Response Escalation
If the user does not respond within a defined period:
Step 1 – send a reminder message.
Step 2 – if there is still no response, send a notification message to the emergency contact.
The delay times should be configurable.

Automated Phone Call Escalation (Optional MVP Feature)
If the user still has not responded after reminder messages, the system may trigger an automated voice call asking the user to confirm their status using keypad input.

Admin Dashboard
Admin users must be able to:
view registered users
see check-in history
see missed check-ins
view alerts sent to contacts
manage user accounts

Subscription Billing
The platform must support monthly subscriptions using Stripe.

Technical Requirements
Developers may propose the stack, but the system will likely include:
SMS provider integration (e.g., Twilio or similar)
backend server for scheduling messages
database to store users and check-in history
webhook handling for incoming SMS replies
Stripe integration for billing
The system should be designed to support scaling to at least 10,000 users.

Proposal Requirements

relevant experience building messaging or SaaS systems
recommended technology stack
estimated timeline
estimated development cost
examples of similar work (if available)

This project is for an MVP focused on core functionality. Simplicity and reliability are the priority.
The client will retain full ownership of all source code and intellectual property.

title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer for AI‑Powered News Feed
description:
--Project Overview--

Ember is a modern platform (Node.js backend, Vercel, Supabase/Postgres, React frontend) serving investment professionals with tools to streamline research and decision-making. We’re embarking on a new AI agent-powered news feed feature that will help financial analysts efficiently track relevant updates in their specific industry sub-sectors. Think of it as a smart, personalized news assistant: it will ingest a “firehose” of news and distill it into the insights that matter most for each user’s niche. We have a clear vision for this system’s capabilities and need a seasoned engineer to help bring it to life.

--Key System Goals & Features:--

Agentic News Aggregation: Design an autonomous agent system that pulls in news from multiple sources – including earnings call transcripts, paywalled financial news sites, social media posts, industry blogs, etc. – ensuring comprehensive coverage of each sector.

Per-Agent Customization: Each agent focuses on a specific sector or topic. The system should support configuring an agent’s focus (e.g. Tech Sector, Healthcare), with the ability to whitelist or blacklist sources and incorporate user feedback to refine relevance over time. In other words, the feed should get smarter and more personalized the more it’s used.

Persistent Memory: Implement storage of collected news content and context so that each agent has “memory.” This allows agents to recognize what’s been seen before, avoid repetition, and provide context-aware summaries. Storing this data (likely in a database or knowledge base) will enable the agent to recall past events when generating new reports.

Automated Recaps: The agents will autonomously generate structured summaries (daily and weekly digests) of the most important news for their sector. An analyst can receive, say, a morning briefing and a weekly round-up tailored to what they care about, instead of sifting through dozens of articles.

Future-Proof Architecture: While the initial goal is a one-way feed from agents to user, we want the architecture to allow future inter-agent communication. Down the line, agents might share insights with each other (for example, a Tech agent alerting a Finance agent about a cross-industry development). Designing with this in mind now will make expansions easier later.

We’re intentionally not prescribing exact implementation details – you will have the freedom to shape the solution (choice of libraries, frameworks, AI integration methods, etc.) as long as the system meets these goals. Our focus is on outcomes: a robust, intelligent news feed that delights users. The project will start with an MVP build (~8–12 weeks) to get a working system in place. If all goes well, there’s a strong possibility for a longer-term collaboration to keep improving and scaling this product.

--Key Responsibilities--

In this role, you will take the lead in engineering this AI-driven news feed from the ground up. Your responsibilities will include:

Architect & Develop the Agent System: Design and implement the core agent-based news feed system on Ember’s platform. This includes defining how agents are structured, how they ingest and process information, and how results are delivered to the frontend. You’ll make high-level architectural decisions (data models, service design, integration points) and then get hands-on in building it.

Multi-Source Data Ingestion: Create robust pipelines to ingest content from diverse sources. Many sources will have public APIs, but others won’t – you’ll need to implement custom web scrapers or crawlers for sites that lack APIs or have anti-scraping measures. The goal is to reliably pull in articles, transcripts, social posts, etc., normalizing them for the agent to analyze. (Some sources may require creative solutions due to dynamic content loading or paywalls – part of the challenge!)

Intelligent Filtering & Deduplication: Develop logic to filter out noise and duplicate information across sources. If the same story appears in multiple outlets, the system should recognize it and avoid bombarding the user. This will likely involve comparing content for similarity and using meta-data. You’ll also incorporate smart filtering rules (for example, removing irrelevant clickbait or low-value content) and plug in user feedback loops – e.g. if a user thumbs-down certain types of stories, the agent should learn and adjust. Over time, the feed should learn the user’s preferences and surface more of what’s useful to them.

LLM Integration (Model-Agnostic): Integrate large language models to power the agents’ understanding and summarization capabilities. The system should be model-agnostic – initially we might use OpenAI’s APIs (GPT-4/3.5), but we want the flexibility to swap in other providers like Anthropic or open-source models down the road. You’ll architect the integration in a modular way (e.g., via an abstraction layer or service) so we’re not locked into a single AI model. The LLM will likely be used to summarize batches of articles and possibly to decide relevance, so experience with prompt design and handling LLM output will be helpful.

Agent Output & Summaries: Ensure each agent can produce clean, structured output for users. This includes generating the daily/weekly recap summaries and possibly real-time alerts for breaking news. You’ll work on how these summaries are formatted and delivered (likely via our React frontend, maybe email notifications in the future). The output should be accurate and concise – part of your job is figuring out how to prompt the model or post-process results to achieve this.

Data Storage & Management: Set up the necessary data storage for this feature – both for incoming content (raw articles, transcripts, etc.) and the agent’s processed results. We use Supabase (Postgres) currently, so you’ll design tables or utilize Supabase’s features to store content and metadata. This stored knowledge will serve as the agent’s “long-term memory” and also allow auditability (e.g., to trace why an agent made a certain summary, we can reference the source data). Scalability and security of this data are important; as we ingest potentially hundreds of articles daily, the solution should remain performant.

Collaboration & Iteration: Work closely with Ember’s founder and product/design team to refine requirements and iterate on the solution. This is a highly collaborative project – for example, you might need to adjust how an agent’s configuration is exposed in the UI or tweak summarization based on user beta testing. You should be comfortable communicating technical trade-offs to non-engineers and incorporating feedback quickly.

Quality, Testing & Deployment: Given the nature of news content and AI, testing will be an ongoing responsibility. You’ll implement checks to ensure the scraping and ingestion are working (no silent failures), possibly write unit/integration tests for the pipeline, and help devise ways to evaluate the quality of the AI summaries (e.g. spot-checking outputs). We are hosted on Vercel, so you’ll also be involved in deploying any backend functions or services you build and monitoring their performance.

Security & Future Compliance: As we build, keep in mind enterprise readiness. In the long run, our target customers may require compliance like SOC 2, so the system should be designed with good security practices from day one. This might include proper handling of API keys and secrets, secure data storage (especially if any news content might be sensitive or behind paywalls), logging and monitoring for the new features, etc. We don’t need full SOC 2 controls in the MVP, but we want a foundation that won’t require a complete rewrite to get there.

Drive the MVP and Beyond: Take ownership of delivering a working MVP of this news feed system within ~8–12 weeks. This includes planning the work, executing on core features, and adapting as requirements evolve. After the MVP, there’s potential to continue iterating on advanced features (like multi-agent interactions, more personalization, scaling to more users, etc.). You would play a key role in that continued development if there’s a mutual fit. In short, you’re not just writing code – you’re leading the technical effort to make this project a success.
